name: Greco-Persian Wars
summary: The Achaemenid Persian Empire fought Athens, Sparta and their allies after the Greek cities of Ionia rebelled against Persian rule. Two great Persian invasions of mainland Greece were defeated at Marathon, Salamis and Plataea, and the Athenian-led Delian League then carried the war to Persian waters. The Greek victory preserved the independence of the city-states and opened the way for the classical age of Athens.

steps.label: 499-494 BC
steps.title: Ionian Revolt
steps.text: The Greek cities of Ionia rose against their Persian-backed tyrants, and Athens and Eretria sent ships to help. The rebels burned Sardis in 498 BC, but Persia slowly recovered the coast and crushed the Ionian fleet off Lade, then sacked Miletus.

moves.label: Ionians and Athenians march on Sardis

battles.name: Battle of Lade
battles.text: The Persian fleet destroyed the Ionian navy after many Samian ships deserted, ending the revolt.

steps.label: 490 BC
steps.title: Marathon
steps.text: Darius I sent a seaborne expedition under Datis and Artaphernes across the Aegean to punish Eretria and Athens. Eretria fell after a siege, but the Athenians and Plataeans defeated the landing force on the plain of Marathon.

moves.label: Datis and Artaphernes cross the Aegean

battles.name: Battle of Marathon
battles.text: Miltiades' hoplites routed the Persian army on the shore and forced the expedition home.

steps.label: 480 BC
steps.title: Xerxes invades
steps.text: Xerxes bridged the Hellespont and led a vast army and fleet along the coast of Thrace and Macedonia. Leonidas and his Spartans held the pass of Thermopylae for three days before being outflanked, and Athens was evacuated and burned. In the narrow straits of Salamis the allied Greek fleet then shattered the Persian navy.

battles.name: Battle of Thermopylae
battles.text: A small Greek force under Leonidas delayed Xerxes' army before being surrounded and destroyed.

battles.name: Battle of Salamis
battles.text: Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into the straits, where the Greek triremes won a decisive victory.

steps.label: 479 BC
steps.title: Plataea and Mycale
steps.text: Xerxes went home but left Mardonius with a picked army in Greece. The united Greek army under the Spartan Pausanias destroyed it at Plataea, while the Greek fleet crossed to Ionia and burned the Persian ships at Mycale.

battles.name: Battle of Plataea
battles.text: Mardonius was killed and his army routed, ending the Persian invasion of Greece.

battles.name: Battle of Mycale
battles.text: Greek forces landed and destroyed the beached Persian fleet and its guard on the Ionian coast.

steps.label: 478-466 BC
steps.title: Delian League offensive
steps.text: Athens organised the Delian League to free the Greek cities of Asia and keep Persia out of the Aegean. Under Cimon the league fleet swept the coast of Asia Minor and won a double victory on land and sea at the Eurymedon river.

battles.name: Battle of the Eurymedon
battles.text: Cimon destroyed a Persian fleet and then its army at the river mouth in Pamphylia.

steps.label: 450-449 BC
steps.title: Cyprus and the Peace of Callias
steps.text: A last Athenian expedition fought in Cyprus, where Cimon died during the siege of Kition. After a victory off Salamis in Cyprus, fighting wound down, and tradition holds that the Peace of Callias recognised the freedom of the Ionian Greeks.

battles.name: Battle of Salamis in Cyprus
battles.text: The Athenians defeated a Phoenician and Cilician fleet and its army near Salamis in Cyprus.

name: Conquests of Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander III of Macedon led a Macedonian and Greek army against the Achaemenid Persian Empire, defeating Darius III in three great battles and taking his capitals. He pushed on through Central Asia to the Indus valley before his troops refused to go further, and he died in Babylon in 323 BC. His conquests spread Greek language and culture across the Near East and began the Hellenistic age.

steps.label: 334 BC
steps.title: Crossing into Asia
steps.text: Alexander crossed the Hellespont with about 40,000 men and met the Persian satraps at the Granicus river. His victory opened western Asia Minor, and he marched down the coast freeing the Greek cities and besieging Halicarnassus.

battles.name: Battle of the Granicus
battles.text: Alexander led his cavalry across the river and routed the army of the western satraps.

steps.label: 333 BC
steps.title: Issus
steps.text: After wintering in Asia Minor and cutting the Gordian knot, Alexander moved through the Cilician Gates to the Syrian coast. Darius III brought the royal army from Babylon and came down behind him, but was routed at Issus and fled, leaving his family in Macedonian hands.

battles.name: Battle of Issus
battles.text: Alexander's charge broke the Persian line and Darius fled the field.

steps.label: 332-331 BC
steps.title: Tyre and Egypt
steps.text: Rather than chase Darius, Alexander secured the Mediterranean coast to neutralise the Persian fleet. Tyre fell after a seven-month siege and a mole built out to the island city, Gaza followed, and Egypt welcomed him as pharaoh. He founded Alexandria and visited the oracle of Ammon at Siwa.

battles.name: Siege of Tyre
battles.text: Alexander built a causeway to the island fortress and stormed it after seven months.

steps.label: 331 BC
steps.title: Gaugamela
steps.text: Alexander marched east across the Euphrates and Tigris to meet the last great army Darius could raise, on open ground chosen for his scythed chariots. Alexander's oblique advance opened a gap in the Persian line and Darius fled again. Babylon and Susa surrendered soon after.

battles.name: Battle of Gaugamela
battles.text: The decisive defeat of Darius III, which effectively ended Achaemenid rule.

steps.label: 330 BC
steps.title: Persepolis and the death of Darius
steps.text: Alexander forced the Persian Gates in the Zagros and took Persepolis, whose palaces were burned. He then pursued Darius through Ecbatana and the Caspian Gates, but the king was murdered by his own satrap Bessus before Alexander could catch him.

battles.name: Battle of the Persian Gate
battles.text: Alexander outflanked the satrap Ariobarzanes holding the mountain pass to Persepolis.

steps.label: 329-327 BC
steps.title: Bactria and Sogdiana
steps.text: Alexander campaigned through Aria and Arachosia, crossed the Hindu Kush and hunted down Bessus. A long guerrilla war followed in Sogdiana under Spitamenes, and on the Jaxartes Alexander defeated the Scythian horsemen. He ended the war by marrying the Sogdian noblewoman Roxana.

moves.label: Through Aria and over the Hindu Kush

battles.name: Battle of the Jaxartes
battles.text: Alexander crossed the river under catapult cover and routed the Scythian horse archers.

steps.label: 327-326 BC
steps.title: India
steps.text: Alexander crossed into the Punjab, where Taxila submitted, and defeated King Porus at the Hydaspes in his last great battle. At the Hyphasis river his exhausted army mutinied and refused to march further east.

battles.name: Battle of the Hydaspes
battles.text: Alexander crossed the swollen river by night and defeated Porus and his war elephants.

steps.label: 325-323 BC
steps.title: Return and death
steps.text: The army sailed and marched down the Indus, then Alexander led part of it through the Gedrosian desert with heavy losses while Nearchus took the fleet along the coast to the Persian Gulf. Back in Babylon, Alexander planned new campaigns but died there in June 323 BC, aged 32.

name: Punic Wars
summary: Rome and Carthage fought three wars for control of the western Mediterranean. Rome won Sicily in the first, survived Hannibal's invasion of Italy to win the second at Zama, and destroyed Carthage itself in the third. The victory made Rome the dominant power of the Mediterranean world.

steps.label: 264-262 BC
steps.title: War for Sicily
steps.text: A dispute over Messana drew Rome across the strait into Sicily, the first time its legions fought outside Italy. Rome won over Syracuse and besieged the Carthaginian base of Agrigentum.

battles.name: Siege of Agrigentum
battles.text: Rome took and sacked Carthage's main base in southern Sicily.

steps.label: 260-255 BC
steps.title: Rome takes to the sea
steps.text: Rome built its first large war fleet and used the corvus boarding bridge to turn sea fights into land battles. After winning at Mylae and Ecnomus, a Roman army under Regulus landed in Africa, but it was destroyed near Tunis by the Spartan mercenary Xanthippus.

battles.name: Battle of Mylae
battles.text: Rome's first great naval victory, won with the corvus boarding bridge.

battles.name: Battle of Cape Ecnomus
battles.text: One of the largest naval battles of antiquity cleared the way to Africa.

battles.name: Battle of Tunis
battles.text: Xanthippus' elephants and cavalry destroyed Regulus' army and captured him.

steps.label: 249-241 BC
steps.title: Aegates Islands
steps.text: The war ground on around the Carthaginian strongholds of western Sicily, where Hamilcar Barca held out on the heights of Eryx. Rome lost a fleet at Drepana, but a new fleet paid for by private citizens destroyed the Carthaginian relief convoy off the Aegates Islands, and Carthage gave up Sicily.

battles.name: Battle of Drepana
battles.text: Carthage's admiral Adherbal destroyed most of the Roman fleet attacking Drepana.

battles.name: Battle of the Aegates
battles.text: Rome's decisive naval victory, which ended the First Punic War.

steps.label: 218 BC
steps.title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
steps.text: Hannibal led an army with war elephants from New Carthage across the Pyrenees, the Rhone and the Alps into the Po valley. Rome had planned to fight in Spain and Africa, but now had to defend Italy, and Hannibal beat the consular armies at the Trebia.

moves.label: Scipio's fleet to Gaul and Spain

battles.name: Battle of the Trebia
battles.text: Hannibal ambushed and destroyed a Roman army on the frozen river in December.

steps.label: 217-216 BC
steps.title: Trasimene and Cannae
steps.text: Hannibal crossed the Apennines and trapped a Roman army on the shore of Lake Trasimene. The next year at Cannae his double envelopment annihilated the largest army Rome had ever fielded, and much of southern Italy, including Capua, went over to Carthage.

battles.name: Battle of Lake Trasimene
battles.text: Hannibal ambushed Flaminius' army in a fog-bound defile by the lake.

battles.name: Battle of Cannae
battles.text: Hannibal's double envelopment killed perhaps 50,000 Romans in a single day.

steps.label: 209-206 BC
steps.title: Rome strikes back
steps.text: Rome refused to make peace and wore Hannibal down in Italy while Publius Cornelius Scipio took the war to Spain. Scipio stormed New Carthage and won at Ilipa, and Hasdrubal's relief army was destroyed at the Metaurus before it could reach his brother.

battles.name: Capture of New Carthage
battles.text: Scipio seized Carthage's capital in Spain with its treasury and arsenal.

battles.name: Battle of the Metaurus
battles.text: Hasdrubal's army was destroyed and his head thrown into Hannibal's camp.

battles.name: Battle of Ilipa
battles.text: Scipio's victory ended Carthaginian power in Spain.

steps.label: 204-202 BC
steps.title: Zama
steps.text: Scipio landed in Africa near Utica and defeated Carthage's armies with the help of the Numidian king Masinissa. Carthage recalled Hannibal from Italy, and at Zama Scipio beat him in the war's final battle, leaving Carthage stripped of its fleet and empire.

battles.name: Battle of Zama
battles.text: Scipio's legions and Numidian cavalry defeated Hannibal and ended the Second Punic War.

steps.label: 149-146 BC
steps.title: Destruction of Carthage
steps.text: Rome, urged on by Cato, seized on a Carthaginian war with Masinissa to send an army to Africa. After a three-year siege, Scipio Aemilianus stormed the city in 146 BC, razed it and made its territory the Roman province of Africa.

battles.name: Siege of Carthage
battles.text: Scipio Aemilianus stormed and destroyed the city after a three-year siege.

name: Qin wars of unification
summary: King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six other Warring States, Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu and Qi, in a decade of campaigns. The victory ended centuries of division, and Ying Zheng proclaimed himself Qin Shi Huang, the First Emperor. The unified state, its laws, script and coinage laid the foundation of imperial China.

steps.label: 230 BC
steps.title: Fall of Han
steps.text: Han, the smallest and weakest of the rival states, lay directly in Qin's path east of the Hangu Pass. The Qin general Neishi Teng took its capital Xinzheng and captured its king, making Han the first state to fall.

battles.name: Capture of Xinzheng
battles.text: Qin seized the Han capital and the Han king, annexing the state.

steps.label: 229-228 BC
steps.title: Conquest of Zhao
steps.text: Wang Jian invaded Zhao from two directions, but was held up by the able Zhao general Li Mu. Qin bribery led the Zhao court to execute Li Mu, and the capital Handan fell in 228 BC; a Zhao prince fled north to set up the remnant state of Dai.

battles.name: Fall of Handan
battles.text: Qin captured the Zhao capital and King Qian of Zhao.

steps.label: 227-226 BC
steps.title: Attack on Yan
steps.text: Prince Dan of Yan sent the assassin Jing Ke to kill the King of Qin, but the attempt failed. Qin retaliated, beat the Yan and Dai armies on the Yi River and took the Yan capital Ji, near modern Beijing, while the Yan king fled to Liaodong.

battles.name: Battle of the Yi River
battles.text: Qin crushed the combined armies of Yan and Dai west of Ji.

steps.label: 225 BC
steps.title: Fall of Wei
steps.text: Wang Ben, son of Wang Jian, besieged the Wei capital Daliang. After three months he diverted the Yellow River and a canal to flood the city, whose walls collapsed, and the King of Wei surrendered.

battles.name: Siege of Daliang
battles.text: Qin flooded the Wei capital, modern Kaifeng, and forced its surrender.

steps.label: 225-223 BC
steps.title: War with Chu
steps.text: Li Xin and Meng Tian invaded Chu with 200,000 men but were routed by the Chu general Xiang Yan. The king then gave the veteran Wang Jian 600,000 men; he waited out Chu in fortified camps, struck as they withdrew, killed Xiang Yan and took the Chu capital Shouchun.

battles.name: Defeat of Li Xin
battles.text: Xiang Yan pursued Li Xin's army for three days and destroyed it near Chengfu.

battles.name: Battle of Qinan
battles.text: Wang Jian destroyed the main Chu army and Xiang Yan was killed.

battles.name: Fall of Shouchun
battles.text: Qin captured the Chu capital and King Fuchu, ending Chu as a state.

steps.label: 222 BC
steps.title: Liaodong, Dai and the south
steps.text: Wang Ben marched to Liaodong and captured the last King of Yan, then turned back to destroy the Zhao remnant state of Dai. In the south, Wang Jian crossed the Yangtze and subdued the old lands of Wu and Yue.

moves.label: Wang Jian south of the Yangtze

steps.label: 221 BC
steps.title: Qi surrenders
steps.text: Qi, the last independent state, had stayed out of the fighting for decades. Wang Ben marched south from Yan and reached its capital Linzi, and King Jian of Qi surrendered without a battle. Ying Zheng took the new title Shi Huangdi, the First Emperor.

name: Early Muslim conquests
summary: After the death of Muhammad, the Rashidun and then Umayyad caliphs led Arab armies out of Arabia against the exhausted Byzantine and Sasanian empires. Within a century the Caliphate stretched from Spain and Morocco to Central Asia and the Indus, though it failed to take Constantinople and was halted in Gaul. The conquests spread Islam and Arabic across a vast region and reshaped the medieval world.

steps.title: Yarmouk and Qadisiyyah
steps.text: Under Caliph Abu Bakr and then Umar, Arab armies invaded Byzantine Syria and Sasanian Iraq at the same time, with Khalid ibn al-Walid making a famous desert march between the fronts. Damascus fell in 634-635, and in 636 Arab victories at the Yarmouk and al-Qadisiyyah broke both empires' field armies.

battles.name: Battle of the Yarmouk
battles.text: A six-day battle that destroyed the Byzantine army and cost the empire Syria.

battles.name: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
battles.text: The Arab victory over the Sasanian general Rostam opened Iraq to conquest.

steps.title: Fall of Persia
steps.text: The Arabs took the Sasanian capital Ctesiphon in 637 and pushed into the Iranian plateau. The victory at Nahavand in 642 ended organised Persian resistance, and the last shah, Yazdegerd III, was killed near Merv in 651.

battles.name: Battle of Nahavand
battles.text: The Victory of Victories destroyed the last great Sasanian army.

steps.title: Egypt
steps.text: Amr ibn al-As led a small army from Palestine across Sinai into Egypt. After victory at Heliopolis and the siege of the Babylon fortress, Alexandria surrendered by treaty in 641-642, giving the Caliphate Egypt's grain and its first fleet bases.

battles.name: Battle of Heliopolis
battles.text: Amr defeated the Byzantine army of Egypt, opening the way to Babylon and Alexandria.

steps.title: North Africa
steps.text: Raids into Byzantine Africa began in 647, and in 670 Uqba ibn Nafi founded Kairouan as a permanent base. Berber resistance was fierce, but Carthage fell in 698 and by about 709 the Umayyads had reached the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

battles.name: Fall of Carthage
battles.text: Hassan ibn al-Numan took Byzantium's last major stronghold in Africa.

steps.title: Spain, Sindh and Transoxiana
steps.text: In 711 Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed the strait that now bears his name and killed the Visigothic king Roderic at the Guadalete, and the Visigothic kingdom collapsed within a few years. In the same years Muhammad ibn Qasim conquered Sindh and Qutayba ibn Muslim took Bukhara and Samarkand.

battles.name: Battle of Guadalete
battles.text: Tariq's army destroyed the Visigothic host and King Roderic was killed.

steps.title: Siege of Constantinople
steps.text: The Umayyads made their greatest effort against the Byzantine capital, sending a huge army under Maslama and a large fleet. Emperor Leo III held the walls, Greek fire burned the Arab ships, and a harsh winter, Bulgar attacks and hunger forced a disastrous retreat.

battles.name: Siege of Constantinople
battles.text: The failed siege saved Byzantium and blocked a Muslim advance into southeastern Europe.

steps.title: Tours
steps.text: The governor of al-Andalus, Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, led a large raid north across the Pyrenees, sacking Bordeaux and heading for the rich abbey of Tours. Charles Martel and the Franks stopped him between Poitiers and Tours, and he was killed in the battle.

battles.name: Battle of Tours
battles.text: The Frankish infantry held firm and the Umayyad commander was killed, ending the raid.

steps.title: Limits of expansion
steps.text: Defeat by the Byzantines at Akroinon, a great Berber revolt in North Africa and setbacks on the Central Asian frontier showed that the age of rapid conquest was over. In 750 the Abbasid revolution overthrew the Umayyad dynasty, and the Caliphate turned from expansion to consolidation.

battles.name: Battle of Akroinon
battles.text: Leo III destroyed a major Umayyad raiding army in western Anatolia.

name: The Crusades
summary: Western European Christians launched a series of armed pilgrimages to win and defend Jerusalem and the Holy Land against the Muslim powers of the Near East. The First Crusade founded the crusader states, but Zengi, Saladin and the Mamluks gradually won them back, and the fall of Acre in 1291 ended the crusader presence. The wars deepened the split between Latin and Greek Christians and widened trade and contact between Europe and the Islamic world.

steps.title: First Crusade
steps.text: Answering Pope Urban II's call, armies of French, Norman and German knights gathered at Constantinople and crossed into Anatolia, defeating the Seljuk Turks at Dorylaeum. After a brutal siege of Antioch they marched down the coast and stormed Jerusalem in July 1099, massacring many of its inhabitants.

battles.name: Battle of Dorylaeum
battles.text: The crusaders defeated Kilij Arslan's Seljuk army and opened the road across Anatolia.

battles.name: Siege of Antioch
battles.text: After taking the city by treachery, the crusaders broke out and routed Kerbogha's relief army.

battles.name: Siege of Jerusalem
battles.text: The crusaders stormed the city and founded the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

steps.title: Second Crusade
steps.text: Zengi, atabeg of Mosul and Aleppo, captured Edessa in 1144, destroying the first crusader state. Louis VII of France and Conrad III of Germany led a new crusade, but both armies suffered badly crossing Anatolia, and their joint siege of Damascus collapsed after four days.

battles.name: Fall of Edessa
battles.text: Zengi's capture of Edessa triggered the Second Crusade.

battles.name: Siege of Damascus
battles.text: The crusader siege failed within days and the crusade broke up.

steps.title: Hattin and the fall of Jerusalem
steps.text: Saladin united Egypt and Syria under Ayyubid rule and invaded the Kingdom of Jerusalem. He lured its army into the waterless hills near Tiberias and destroyed it at the Horns of Hattin, then took Jerusalem and most of the kingdom's towns.

battles.name: Battle of Hattin
battles.text: Saladin destroyed the crusader field army and captured King Guy.

battles.name: Siege of Jerusalem
battles.text: Jerusalem surrendered to Saladin after a short siege.

steps.title: Third Crusade
steps.text: Frederick Barbarossa led a German army across Anatolia but drowned in the Saleph river. Richard I of England and Philip II of France arrived by sea and took Acre after a two-year siege, and Richard beat Saladin at Arsuf, but neither side could win outright and a truce left Jerusalem in Muslim hands.

battles.name: Siege of Acre
battles.text: The crusaders captured Acre, which became the new capital of the kingdom.

battles.name: Battle of Arsuf
battles.text: Richard's disciplined march held off Saladin's attacks and then routed his army.

steps.title: Fourth Crusade
steps.text: Short of money to pay Venice for its fleet, the crusaders were diverted first to Zara and then to Constantinople to restore a Byzantine claimant. In 1204 they stormed and sacked the Christian city and set up a Latin Empire there instead of going on to the Holy Land.

battles.name: Sack of Constantinople
battles.text: Crusaders stormed the Byzantine capital and plundered it for three days.

steps.title: Crusades against Egypt
steps.text: Seeing Egypt as the key to Jerusalem, the Fifth Crusade took Damietta in 1219 but was trapped by the Nile flood. Louis IX of France tried again in 1249, took Damietta and advanced on Cairo, but his army was defeated at Mansurah and he was captured.

battles.name: Siege of Damietta
battles.text: The Fifth Crusade took the Nile port after an eighteen-month siege.

battles.name: Battle of Mansurah
battles.text: Ayyubid and Mamluk troops destroyed the crusader vanguard, leading to Louis IX's capture.

steps.title: Mamluks and the fall of Acre
steps.text: The Mamluk sultans of Egypt, having stopped the Mongols, turned on the remaining crusader towns. Baibars took Antioch in 1268, and in 1291 Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil besieged and stormed Acre, ending two centuries of crusader states in the Levant.

battles.name: Siege of Antioch
battles.text: Baibars captured and destroyed the crusader Principality of Antioch.

battles.name: Siege of Acre
battles.text: The Mamluks stormed the last great crusader city, ending the crusader states.

name: Mongol conquests
summary: Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes in 1206 and launched campaigns that his sons and grandsons carried across Eurasia, from Korea and China to Russia, Poland and the Middle East. Mobile horse archers, ruthless sieges and terror built the largest contiguous land empire in history, though Mamluk Egypt, Japan and Vietnam held them off. The conquests killed millions but also linked East and West through trade and travel along the Silk Road.

steps.title: Genghis Khan and the Jin
steps.text: Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan in 1206 and first forced Western Xia to submit. In 1211 he invaded the Jurchen Jin empire of northern China, destroying its army at Yehuling, and in 1215 the Jin capital Zhongdu fell.

battles.name: Battle of Yehuling
battles.text: The Mongols routed a huge Jin army at the Badger Mouth pass.

battles.name: Fall of Zhongdu
battles.text: The Mongols took and sacked the Jin capital near modern Beijing.

steps.title: Destruction of Khwarazm
steps.text: After the Khwarazm Shah's governor at Otrar massacred a Mongol trade caravan, Genghis Khan invaded Central Asia and destroyed the great cities of Bukhara, Samarkand, Merv and Nishapur. Jebe and Subutai then rode around the Caspian Sea and defeated the Rus princes and Cumans on the Kalka.

battles.name: Siege of Samarkand
battles.text: The Khwarazmian capital surrendered after a short siege.

battles.name: Battle of the Indus
battles.text: Genghis Khan destroyed the army of Jalal al-Din on the banks of the Indus.

battles.name: Battle of the Kalka River
battles.text: Jebe and Subutai crushed an army of Rus princes and Cumans.

steps.title: Fall of the Jin
steps.text: Western Xia was destroyed in 1227, the year Genghis Khan died. His successor Ogedei renewed the war on the Jin, while Tolui led a flanking march through Song territory and won at Sanfengshan; the last Jin emperor died at Caizhou in 1234.

battles.name: Battle of Sanfengshan
battles.text: Tolui destroyed the last major Jin field army in a snowstorm.

battles.name: Siege of Caizhou
battles.text: Mongols and Song allies took the last Jin refuge, ending the dynasty.

steps.title: Invasion of Europe
steps.text: Batu and Subutai conquered the Volga Bulgars and destroyed the principalities of Rus, sacking Ryazan, Vladimir and Kiev. In 1241 two Mongol armies struck Poland and Hungary, winning at Legnica and Mohi, but they withdrew in 1242 after news of Ogedei's death.

battles.name: Siege of Kiev
battles.text: The Mongols stormed and devastated the old capital of Rus.

battles.name: Battle of Legnica
battles.text: A Mongol detachment destroyed the army of Henry II of Silesia.

battles.name: Battle of Mohi
battles.text: Batu and Subutai annihilated the army of King Bela IV of Hungary.

steps.title: Hulagu in the Middle East
steps.text: Mongke sent his brother Hulagu west; he destroyed the Assassin fortresses of Alamut and in 1258 sacked Baghdad, killing the last Abbasid caliph. When Hulagu withdrew most of his army, the Mamluks of Egypt defeated the force he left behind at Ain Jalut.

battles.name: Siege of Baghdad
battles.text: Hulagu sacked the Abbasid capital and ended the caliphate there.

battles.name: Battle of Ain Jalut
battles.text: The Mamluks dealt the Mongols their first major defeat and saved Egypt.

steps.title: Conquest of the Song
steps.text: Kublai Khan, founder of the Yuan dynasty, took the fortress twin cities of Xiangyang and Fancheng after a five-year siege using Persian counterweight trebuchets. Bayan then sailed and marched down the Yangtze to take the Song capital Lin'an, and the last Song loyalists were destroyed at sea off Yamen in 1279.

battles.name: Siege of Xiangyang
battles.text: The fall of the key fortress opened the Yangtze to the Mongols.

battles.name: Battle of Yamen
battles.text: The Yuan fleet destroyed the last Song court and fleet.

steps.title: The limits of conquest
steps.text: Kublai's two invasions of Japan in 1274 and 1281 were repulsed by samurai defences and destroyed by storms, the kamikaze. Invasions of Dai Viet ended in defeat on the Bach Dang river in 1288, and after Kublai's death in 1294 the empire had stopped expanding.

battles.name: Invasion of Hakata Bay
battles.text: Japanese defenders held the coast until a typhoon wrecked the Mongol fleet.

battles.name: Battle of Bach Dang
battles.text: Tran Hung Dao trapped the Yuan fleet on stakes planted in the river.

name: Hundred Years' War
summary: The Plantagenet kings of England and the Valois kings of France fought for over a century over English lands in France and the English claim to the French throne. English longbowmen won great victories at Crecy, Poitiers and Agincourt, but France recovered under Charles V and again after Joan of Arc, and by 1453 England held only Calais. The war strengthened royal power and national identity in both countries.

steps.title: War at sea
steps.text: Philip VI confiscated Edward III's duchy of Aquitaine, and Edward claimed the French crown through his mother. The first great clash came at sea, where the English fleet destroyed the French navy in the harbour of Sluys and won control of the Channel.

battles.name: Battle of Sluys
battles.text: English archers and men-at-arms destroyed the French fleet at anchor.

steps.title: Crecy and Calais
steps.text: Edward III landed in Normandy, sacked Caen and marched toward Flanders with Philip VI in pursuit. At Crecy the English longbowmen shattered repeated French cavalry charges, and Edward went on to besiege and take Calais, which England held for two centuries.

battles.name: Battle of Crecy
battles.text: English longbows and dismounted knights crushed the French army.

battles.name: Siege of Calais
battles.text: Calais surrendered after an eleven-month siege.

steps.title: Poitiers
steps.text: Edward the Black Prince led destructive raids from English Gascony. Caught near Poitiers by King John II, he won a crushing victory and captured the French king, leading to the Treaty of Bretigny in 1360, which gave England a greatly enlarged Aquitaine.

battles.name: Battle of Poitiers
battles.text: The Black Prince defeated and captured John II of France.

steps.title: French recovery
steps.text: Charles V renewed the war and, guided by Bertrand du Guesclin, avoided pitched battles while retaking towns one by one. A Castilian fleet allied to France destroyed an English fleet off La Rochelle, and by 1380 England held little beyond Calais, Bordeaux and Bayonne.

battles.name: Battle of La Rochelle
battles.text: A Castilian fleet allied to France destroyed an English fleet and its pay chests.

steps.title: Agincourt
steps.text: Henry V revived the war while France was torn by civil war between Armagnacs and Burgundians. After taking Harfleur he marched for Calais and won an astonishing victory at Agincourt, then conquered Normandy, and the Treaty of Troyes in 1420 made him heir to the French throne.

battles.name: Battle of Agincourt
battles.text: Henry V's archers destroyed a much larger French army in the mud.

steps.title: Joan of Arc
steps.text: The English and Burgundians besieged Orleans, the gateway to the south still loyal to the Dauphin Charles. Joan of Arc helped lift the siege, the French routed the English at Patay, and Charles was crowned at Reims, turning the tide of the war.

moves.label: March to the coronation at Reims

battles.name: Siege of Orleans
battles.text: Joan of Arc's relief force broke the English siege in nine days.

battles.name: Battle of Patay
battles.text: French cavalry caught the English archers before they could deploy.

steps.title: Expulsion of the English
steps.text: After the Burgundians made peace with Charles VII in 1435, the French reformed their army and built a powerful artillery train. They reconquered Normandy after victory at Formigny, then Gascony, and the defeat of John Talbot at Castillon in 1453 ended the war.

battles.name: Battle of Formigny
battles.text: French troops and cannon destroyed the English relief army in Normandy.

battles.name: Battle of Castillon
battles.text: French artillery killed Talbot and broke the last English army in Gascony.

name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec and Inca empires
summary: Small bands of Spanish conquistadors under Hernan Cortes and Francisco Pizarro overthrew the two greatest states of the Americas. Steel, horses and guns mattered, but so did tens of thousands of native allies, European diseases such as smallpox, and the Inca civil war. The conquests founded Spain's American empire and its flow of silver, and devastated the native peoples.

steps.title: Cortes lands in Mexico
steps.text: Hernan Cortes sailed from Cuba with about 500 men, landed on the Gulf coast and founded Veracruz. Allied with the Totonacs and, after hard fighting, with Tlaxcala, he marched inland and was received by Moctezuma II in Tenochtitlan, where he soon took the emperor hostage.

steps.title: Noche Triste and Otumba
steps.text: Cortes left the capital to defeat a rival Spanish force under Narvaez on the coast. A massacre of Aztec nobles by the men he left behind provoked a revolt, Moctezuma was killed, and the Spanish fought their way out of the city on the Noche Triste with heavy losses, before beating an Aztec army at Otumba on the way to Tlaxcala.

battles.name: Noche Triste
battles.text: The Spanish lost hundreds of men and most of their treasure fleeing along the causeways.

battles.name: Battle of Otumba
battles.text: Cortes' cavalry charge killed the Aztec commander and broke the army blocking his retreat.

steps.title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
steps.text: Rebuilt with Tlaxcalan and other native allies, Cortes based himself at Texcoco and launched brigantines onto the lake to cut the island city off. After a 75-day siege, worsened by a smallpox epidemic, Cuauhtemoc was captured and Tenochtitlan fell in August 1521.

battles.name: Siege of Tenochtitlan
battles.text: The Spanish and their allies starved and stormed the Aztec capital.

steps.title: Pizarro and Cajamarca
steps.text: Francisco Pizarro sailed from Panama with fewer than 200 men as the Inca Empire emerged from a civil war won by Atahualpa over his brother Huascar. At Cajamarca the Spanish ambushed Atahualpa's escort and seized the emperor, who was later executed despite paying a huge ransom in gold and silver.

battles.name: Battle of Cajamarca
battles.text: Pizarro's surprise attack killed thousands of Atahualpa's attendants and captured the emperor.

steps.title: Cuzco
steps.text: After Atahualpa's execution, Pizarro marched south through Jauja toward the Inca capital, fighting off the army of the general Quisquis. Despite a sharp setback at Vilcaconga, the Spanish entered Cuzco in November 1533 and installed Manco Inca as a puppet ruler.

battles.name: Battle of Vilcaconga
battles.text: Inca troops ambushed the Spanish vanguard on a steep slope near Cuzco.

battles.name: Capture of Cuzco
battles.text: Pizarro occupied the Inca capital and crowned Manco Inca as his puppet.

name: Thirty Years' War
summary: A Protestant revolt in Bohemia against the Catholic Habsburg emperor grew into a European war fought mostly in Germany, drawing in Denmark, Sweden, France and Spain. Armies and the famine and plague they spread killed perhaps a third of the population in parts of Germany. The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 confirmed the independence of the German princes and is often seen as the start of the modern state system.

steps.title: Bohemian revolt
steps.text: Protestant nobles threw the emperor's regents out of a window in Prague and chose Frederick V of the Palatinate as king of Bohemia. Emperor Ferdinand II and Maximilian of Bavaria's Catholic League sent an army that crushed the rebels at White Mountain outside Prague.

battles.name: Battle of White Mountain
battles.text: Tilly's army routed the Bohemian rebels in two hours and Frederick V fled.

steps.title: Danish phase
steps.text: Christian IV of Denmark entered the war to defend the Protestant north. Wallenstein's new imperial army beat Mansfeld at the Dessau Bridge and Tilly crushed the Danes at Lutter, though Wallenstein failed to take Stralsund, and the emperor's Edict of Restitution of 1629 alarmed all Protestants.

battles.name: Battle of Dessau Bridge
battles.text: Wallenstein repulsed Mansfeld's assault on the Elbe crossing.

battles.name: Battle of Lutter
battles.text: Tilly decisively defeated Christian IV, knocking Denmark out of the war.

battles.name: Siege of Stralsund
battles.text: Danish and Swedish help kept Wallenstein from taking the Baltic port.

steps.title: Sweden enters
steps.text: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden landed in Pomerania with a modern, mobile army. After Tilly's troops sacked Magdeburg, Saxony joined Sweden, and at Breitenfeld Gustavus won the first great Protestant victory of the war.

battles.name: Sack of Magdeburg
battles.text: Imperial troops stormed the Protestant city, and most of its people died.

battles.name: Battle of Breitenfeld
battles.text: Gustavus Adolphus' flexible brigades destroyed Tilly's veteran army.

steps.title: Gustavus in Germany
steps.text: Gustavus swept across Germany to the Rhine and then into Bavaria, where Tilly was mortally wounded at the Lech. The recalled Wallenstein moved into Saxony, and at Lutzen the Swedes won the field but Gustavus Adolphus was killed.

battles.name: Battle of Rain
battles.text: Gustavus forced the crossing of the Lech and Tilly was mortally wounded.

battles.name: Battle of Lutzen
battles.text: The Swedes drove Wallenstein from the field, but Gustavus Adolphus was killed.

steps.title: Nordlingen
steps.text: Wallenstein was murdered on the emperor's orders in 1634. A Spanish army came over the Alps from Milan to join the imperial forces, and together they shattered the Swedish army at Nordlingen, after which Saxony and most German Protestant states made the Peace of Prague with the emperor.

battles.name: Battle of Nordlingen
battles.text: Spanish and imperial forces destroyed the main Swedish army in southern Germany.

steps.title: France enters
steps.text: Cardinal Richelieu brought Catholic France into the war against the Habsburgs in 1635 to stop their encirclement of France. Sweden recovered with a victory at Wittstock, and in 1643 the young Duke of Enghien broke the famous Spanish tercios at Rocroi.

battles.name: Battle of Wittstock
battles.text: Baner's Swedes defeated the imperial and Saxon army in Brandenburg.

battles.name: Battle of Rocroi
battles.text: The French broke the Spanish infantry, ending its reputation for invincibility.

steps.title: Peace of Westphalia
steps.text: Torstensson's Swedes destroyed an imperial army at Jankau and advanced toward Vienna, while French and Swedish forces ravaged Bavaria. After years of talks at Munster and Osnabruck, the Peace of Westphalia ended the war in October 1648.

battles.name: Battle of Jankau
battles.text: Torstensson's Swedes destroyed the emperor's last major army in Bohemia.

battles.name: Battle of Zusmarshausen
battles.text: French and Swedish troops defeated the last imperial and Bavarian field army.

name: Seven Years' War
summary: Britain and Prussia fought France, Austria, Russia, Sweden and later Spain in a war that spanned Europe, North America, the Caribbean, West Africa and India. Prussia survived and kept Silesia, while Britain took New France and won dominance in India, emerging as the leading colonial and naval power. The war's enormous debts helped set the stage for the American and French revolutions.

steps.title: War opens in Minorca and Saxony
steps.text: A French expedition seized British-held Minorca after Admiral Byng failed to relieve it, and Byng was later executed. In August Frederick II of Prussia struck first, invading Saxony, beating an Austrian relief army and forcing the Saxon army to surrender at Pirna.

battles.name: Siege of Fort St Philip
battles.text: The French captured Minorca's fortress after the British relief fleet withdrew.

battles.name: Battle of Lobositz
battles.text: Frederick turned back an Austrian army marching to rescue the trapped Saxons.

steps.title: Frederick's year of battles
steps.text: Frederick invaded Bohemia but was beaten at Kolin and fell back as French, Austrian, Russian and Swedish armies closed in. He then marched west to rout a Franco-Imperial army at Rossbach and raced east to crush the Austrians at Leuthen, saving Prussia.

battles.name: Battle of Kolin
battles.text: Daun's Austrians repulsed Frederick's attack, forcing him to abandon the siege of Prague.

battles.name: Battle of Rossbach
battles.text: Frederick routed a much larger French and Imperial army in about ninety minutes.

battles.name: Battle of Leuthen
battles.text: Frederick's oblique attack shattered the Austrian army and recovered most of Silesia.

steps.title: Struggle for India
steps.text: Robert Clive's East India Company force retook Calcutta and defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, laying the foundation of British rule in Bengal. In the south British forces defeated the French under Lally and captured Pondicherry, ending French hopes of an Indian empire.

battles.name: Battle of Plassey
battles.text: Clive defeated Siraj ud-Daulah after key Bengali commanders held back, giving the Company control of Bengal.

battles.name: Battle of Wandiwash
battles.text: Eyre Coote decisively defeated Lally's French army in the Carnatic.

battles.name: Siege of Pondicherry
battles.text: The main French base in India surrendered after a long siege.

steps.title: War for North America
steps.text: Britain poured troops and ships into the fight for New France under William Pitt's direction. An amphibious force captured the fortress of Louisbourg, opening the St Lawrence, but a far larger British army was bloodily repulsed by Montcalm at Fort Carillon.

battles.name: Siege of Louisbourg
battles.text: British forces took the great French fortress on Cape Breton Island after a seven-week siege.

battles.name: Battle of Carillon
battles.text: Montcalm's outnumbered French beat off repeated British assaults at Ticonderoga.

steps.title: Year of Victories
steps.text: Britain's annus mirabilis brought victory on several continents. Wolfe's army took Quebec, an Anglo-German army beat the French at Minden, and Hawke's fleet destroyed the French navy at Quiberon Bay, ending French invasion plans.

moves.label: Wolfe's expedition up the St Lawrence

battles.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
battles.text: Wolfe defeated Montcalm outside Quebec, and both commanders died of their wounds.

battles.name: Battle of Minden
battles.text: Ferdinand of Brunswick's allied army routed the French, keeping them out of Hanover.

battles.name: Battle of Quiberon Bay
battles.text: Hawke chased the French fleet into a rocky bay in a gale and destroyed it.

steps.title: Prussia on the brink
steps.text: A Russian and Austrian army destroyed Frederick's army at Kunersdorf, and Russian and Austrian troops briefly occupied Berlin in 1760. Frederick fought on with dwindling resources, winning a costly victory at Torgau, while British forces completed the conquest of Canada with the fall of Montreal.

battles.name: Battle of Kunersdorf
battles.text: Saltykov and Laudon inflicted Frederick's worst defeat, nearly destroying his army.

battles.name: Battle of Torgau
battles.text: Frederick won a narrow and very bloody victory that kept Saxony in play.

steps.title: Russia changes sides; Spain enters
steps.text: The death of Empress Elizabeth brought Peter III to the Russian throne, and he made peace with Prussia, saving Frederick. Spain joined France, and Britain answered by capturing Havana and Manila, Spain's key ports in the Caribbean and Asia.

moves.label: British expedition via the Old Bahama Channel

battles.name: Siege of Havana
battles.text: A British army and fleet captured Havana after a two-month siege.

battles.name: Battle of Manila
battles.text: A British force from Madras stormed Manila, the capital of the Spanish Philippines.

steps.label: Feb 1763
steps.title: Treaties of Paris and Hubertusburg
steps.text: In the Treaty of Paris France ceded Canada and its lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, Spain gave up Florida in exchange for Havana and Manila, and France handed Louisiana to Spain. At Hubertusburg Austria accepted Prussia's possession of Silesia, confirming Prussia as a great power.

name: American Revolutionary War
summary: Thirteen British colonies in North America rebelled against Parliament's taxes and authority, declared independence in 1776 and fought Britain and its Loyalist and German allies. With decisive help from France, and later Spain and the Dutch Republic, the Americans forced a British surrender at Yorktown. The Treaty of Paris recognised the United States, whose republican experiment inspired revolutions in Europe and Latin America.

steps.label: Apr-Jun 1775
steps.title: Lexington, Concord and Bunker Hill
steps.text: British regulars marched from Boston to seize militia supplies at Concord and were harried all the way back by thousands of colonial militiamen. The militia then besieged Boston, and the British took Breed's and Bunker Hill only at a terrible cost.

battles.name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
battles.text: Militia drove the British column back to Boston, opening the war.

battles.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
battles.text: The British captured the heights but lost over a thousand men killed or wounded.

steps.label: Jul 1776-Jan 1777
steps.title: Independence and the New York campaign
steps.text: Congress declared independence on 4 July 1776 as a huge British army and fleet arrived at New York. Howe drove Washington from Long Island and Manhattan and across New Jersey, but Washington struck back across the Delaware at Trenton and Princeton.

battles.name: Battle of Long Island
battles.text: Howe outflanked Washington's army in Brooklyn in the largest battle of the war.

battles.name: Battle of Trenton
battles.text: Washington surprised and captured the Hessian garrison after crossing the icy Delaware.

steps.title: Saratoga and Philadelphia
steps.text: Burgoyne pushed south from Canada down Lake Champlain while Howe sailed to the Chesapeake and took Philadelphia after beating Washington at Brandywine. Burgoyne's army, isolated in upstate New York, was surrounded and surrendered at Saratoga.

battles.name: Battles of Saratoga
battles.text: Gates and Arnold defeated Burgoyne, whose surrender brought France into the war.

battles.name: Battle of Brandywine
battles.text: Howe flanked Washington's army and opened the road to Philadelphia.

steps.title: France enters the war
steps.text: After Saratoga France signed an alliance with the United States, turning the rebellion into a global war. Washington's army, retrained at Valley Forge, fought the British to a draw at Monmouth as they withdrew from Philadelphia to New York.

battles.name: Battle of Monmouth
battles.text: A long, hot battle ended without a clear winner, but showed the Continental Army's new discipline.

steps.title: The war moves south
steps.text: Hoping to rally Loyalists, Britain shifted its effort to the South, taking Savannah and then Charleston with its entire American garrison. Cornwallis routed an American army at Camden, but frontier militia destroyed a Loyalist force at Kings Mountain.

battles.name: Siege of Charleston
battles.text: Some 5,000 American troops surrendered, the worst American defeat of the war.

battles.name: Battle of Camden
battles.text: Cornwallis routed Gates's army in South Carolina.

battles.name: Battle of Kings Mountain
battles.text: Patriot frontier militia wiped out Ferguson's Loyalist force.

steps.label: Jan-May 1781
steps.title: Carolinas campaign
steps.text: Nathanael Greene split his army and wore down the British; Daniel Morgan won a brilliant victory at Cowpens. Cornwallis won at Guilford Court House but lost a quarter of his army, and he marched into Virginia.

battles.name: Battle of Cowpens
battles.text: Morgan's double envelopment destroyed Tarleton's British force.

battles.name: Battle of Guilford Court House
battles.text: Cornwallis held the field but his losses crippled the campaign.

steps.label: Sep-Oct 1781
steps.title: Yorktown
steps.text: Washington and Rochambeau marched their armies from New York to Virginia while de Grasse's French fleet sailed from the Caribbean and drove off the British fleet at the Battle of the Chesapeake. Trapped at Yorktown, Cornwallis surrendered his army on 19 October 1781.

moves.label: De Grasse's fleet from the Caribbean

battles.name: Battle of the Chesapeake
battles.text: De Grasse turned back the British fleet, sealing Cornwallis off from rescue by sea.

battles.name: Siege of Yorktown
battles.text: Cornwallis surrendered about 8,000 men, effectively ending major fighting in America.

steps.title: Global war and the Treaty of Paris
steps.text: Fighting continued at sea and around Europe, where Britain beat the French fleet at the Saintes and held Gibraltar against a great Franco-Spanish siege. The Treaty of Paris in September 1783 recognised American independence with a western border on the Mississippi.

battles.name: Battle of the Saintes
battles.text: Rodney's fleet defeated de Grasse and captured him, protecting Jamaica.

battles.name: Great Siege of Gibraltar
battles.text: The British garrison repulsed the great Franco-Spanish assault with floating batteries.

name: Napoleonic Wars
summary: Napoleon's French Empire and its allies fought a series of coalitions led by Britain with Austria, Russia, Prussia, Spain, Portugal and others. Napoleon dominated continental Europe until the disaster in Russia in 1812, after which he was defeated in 1814 and finally at Waterloo in 1815. The wars spread French legal and administrative reforms, stirred nationalism and left Britain the leading world power.

steps.label: Aug-Oct 1805
steps.title: From Boulogne to Ulm, and Trafalgar
steps.text: Britain had resumed war in 1803, and Napoleon massed an invasion army at Boulogne. When Austria and Russia joined a Third Coalition, he swung the army to the Danube and trapped an Austrian army at Ulm, but a day later Nelson destroyed the Franco-Spanish fleet off Cape Trafalgar.

battles.name: Ulm campaign
battles.text: Mack surrendered an Austrian army of about 25,000 after being encircled.

battles.name: Battle of Trafalgar
battles.text: Nelson's fleet destroyed the Franco-Spanish fleet, ending any French threat to invade Britain.

steps.label: Nov-Dec 1805
steps.title: Austerlitz
steps.text: Napoleon occupied Vienna and moved north into Moravia, luring the Russian and Austrian armies into attacking him. His victory at Austerlitz broke the Third Coalition and Austria made peace at Pressburg.

battles.name: Battle of Austerlitz
battles.text: Napoleon split the allied centre on the Pratzen Heights in his most celebrated victory.

steps.label: Oct 1806-Jul 1807
steps.title: Prussia and Russia defeated
steps.text: Prussia went to war and was crushed in a single day at Jena and Auerstedt, and Napoleon entered Berlin. The campaign moved into Poland and East Prussia, where a bloody draw at Eylau was followed by victory at Friedland and the Treaties of Tilsit with Russia.

battles.name: Battle of Jena-Auerstedt
battles.text: Twin French victories destroyed the Prussian army in a day.

battles.name: Battle of Eylau
battles.text: A savage battle in a snowstorm ended with both armies exhausted.

battles.name: Battle of Friedland
battles.text: Napoleon routed Bennigsen's Russians, forcing the Tsar to make peace at Tilsit.

steps.title: Spain rises; Wagram
steps.text: Napoleon put his brother Joseph on the Spanish throne, provoking a national uprising and a long war in Iberia backed by Britain. Austria rejoined the fight in 1809 and beat Napoleon at Aspern-Essling, but was defeated at Wagram weeks later.

battles.name: Battle of Bailen
battles.text: A Spanish army forced Dupont's corps to surrender, the first major defeat of a Napoleonic army.

battles.name: Battle of Aspern-Essling
battles.text: Archduke Charles threw Napoleon back across the Danube, his first personal defeat in a decade.

battles.name: Battle of Wagram
battles.text: Napoleon defeated the Austrians in a huge two-day battle, forcing another peace.

steps.title: Wellington in the Peninsula
steps.text: Massena's invasion of Portugal stalled before Wellington's fortified Lines of Torres Vedras, and Spanish guerrillas tied down large French forces. In 1812 Wellington took the border fortresses, won at Salamanca and briefly entered Madrid.

battles.name: Battle of Bussaco
battles.text: Wellington repulsed Massena's frontal attacks on a ridge before withdrawing to his lines.

battles.name: Battle of Salamanca
battles.text: Wellington routed Marmont's army in a swift flank attack.

steps.label: Jun-Dec 1812
steps.title: Invasion of Russia
steps.text: Napoleon crossed the Niemen with over 600,000 men. The Russians retreated, fought a huge battle at Borodino and abandoned Moscow, which burned; when the Tsar refused to negotiate, the Grande Armee retreated through the winter and was almost destroyed.

battles.name: Battle of Borodino
battles.text: The bloodiest single day of the wars left the French in possession of the field and the road to Moscow open.

battles.name: Battle of the Berezina
battles.text: Napoleon escaped across the river on improvised bridges but lost tens of thousands of men and stragglers.

steps.title: Leipzig and the fall of Paris
steps.text: Prussia, Austria and Sweden joined Russia and Britain, and the coalition beat Napoleon in the Battle of the Nations at Leipzig. Wellington drove the French out of Spain after Vitoria, the allies invaded France, Paris fell and Napoleon abdicated and was exiled to Elba.

battles.name: Battle of Vitoria
battles.text: Wellington broke Joseph Bonaparte's army and ended French rule in Spain.

battles.name: Battle of Leipzig
battles.text: The Battle of the Nations, the largest in Europe before 1914, drove Napoleon out of Germany.

battles.name: Battle of Paris
battles.text: The allies stormed the heights around Paris and the city capitulated.

steps.label: Mar-Jun 1815
steps.title: The Hundred Days and Waterloo
steps.text: Napoleon escaped from Elba, landed in southern France and marched on Paris as the army rallied to him. He invaded Belgium, beat the Prussians at Ligny, but was decisively defeated at Waterloo by Wellington and Blucher and exiled to Saint Helena; the Congress of Vienna redrew Europe.

battles.name: Battle of Ligny
battles.text: Napoleon defeated Blucher, but the Prussian army withdrew intact.

battles.name: Battle of Waterloo
battles.text: Wellington's army held until the Prussians arrived, and Napoleon's army collapsed.

name: Taiping Rebellion
summary: Hong Xiuquan, who believed he was the younger brother of Jesus, led the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom in a revolt against the Qing dynasty that captured Nanjing and much of the Yangtze valley. Regional Qing armies such as Zeng Guofan's Xiang Army, aided late in the war by Western-officered forces, crushed the rebellion in 1864. With perhaps 20 to 30 million dead it was one of the deadliest wars in history, and it shifted power from the Qing court to regional strongmen.

steps.label: Jan 1851
steps.title: The Jintian Uprising
steps.text: Hong Xiuquan's God Worshipping Society gathered thousands of followers in Guangxi and defeated Qing troops sent against them. In January 1851 Hong proclaimed the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, and the rebels moved north to Yong'an.

battles.name: Jintian Uprising
battles.text: The rebels beat off Qing forces and proclaimed their Heavenly Kingdom.

steps.title: March to Nanjing
steps.text: Breaking out of Yong'an, the Taiping marched north through Hunan, failing to take Changsha but gathering huge numbers of recruits. They seized Wuchang, sailed down the Yangtze and captured Nanjing in March 1853, making it their Heavenly Capital.

battles.name: Siege of Changsha
battles.text: The Qing garrison held the city and the Taiping leader Xiao Chaogui was killed.

battles.name: Capture of Wuchang
battles.text: The Taiping took their first provincial capital and its river fleet.

battles.name: Capture of Nanjing
battles.text: Nanjing fell and became the Taiping capital, Tianjing.

steps.title: Northern and Western Expeditions
steps.text: A Taiping army marched north to take Beijing, reached the outskirts of Tianjin, but was destroyed by Qing cavalry under Senggelinqin. A Western Expedition fought up the Yangtze against Zeng Guofan's new Hunan army, the Xiang Army, and won a major victory at Hukou.

battles.name: Fall of Lianzhen
battles.text: Senggelinqin captured the last Northern Expedition leaders and ended the threat to Beijing.

battles.name: Battle of Hukou
battles.text: The Taiping trapped and smashed Zeng Guofan's river fleet at the mouth of Poyang Lake.

steps.title: Victory and the Tianjing Incident
steps.text: The Taiping broke the Qing Jiangnan Great Camp besieging Nanjing, reaching the height of their power. Weeks later a power struggle in Nanjing, the Tianjing Incident, saw the Eastern King Yang Xiuqing and thousands of his followers killed, and the able general Shi Dakai later left with his army.

battles.name: Jiangnan Great Camp
battles.text: Taiping armies destroyed the Qing siege camp east of Nanjing.

steps.title: Revival under Li Xiucheng
steps.text: New commanders Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng restored Taiping fortunes, wiping out a Xiang Army force at Sanhe. In 1860 they broke the rebuilt Qing siege of Nanjing and swept east to take Suzhou, but were turned back at Shanghai.

battles.name: Battle of Sanhe
battles.text: Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng annihilated Li Xubin's Xiang Army force.

battles.name: Capture of Suzhou
battles.text: The Taiping captured the rich city of Suzhou after breaking the Jiangnan siege.

battles.name: Defence of Shanghai
battles.text: Qing troops and Western forces defended Shanghai against Li Xiucheng.

steps.title: Anqing falls; Shanghai holds
steps.text: Zeng Guofan's brother Zeng Guoquan took Anqing in 1861, opening the way down the Yangtze to Nanjing. Li Hongzhang's Huai Army and the Ever Victorious Army, later led by Charles Gordon, defended Shanghai and recaptured towns around it, including Suzhou in late 1863.

moves.label: Huai Army and Ever Victorious Army

battles.name: Siege of Anqing
battles.text: The Xiang Army starved Anqing into surrender, a decisive turning point.

battles.name: Recapture of Suzhou
battles.text: Li Hongzhang and Gordon's forces retook Suzhou, and the surrendered Taiping leaders were executed.

steps.label: Jun-Jul 1864
steps.title: Fall of Nanjing
steps.text: With Nanjing encircled and starving, Hong Xiuquan died in June 1864. The Xiang Army breached the walls in July and massacred much of the population, and remaining Taiping bands were hunted down over the next few years.

battles.name: Third Battle of Nanjing
battles.text: The Xiang Army stormed the Taiping capital and ended the Heavenly Kingdom.

name: American Civil War
summary: Eleven Southern slave states seceded after Abraham Lincoln's election and formed the Confederacy, which fought the United States government (the Union). After four years and some 620,000 or more military deaths, the Union's greater industry and manpower prevailed. The war preserved the United States and ended slavery through the Thirteenth Amendment.

steps.label: Apr-Jul 1861
steps.title: Fort Sumter and First Bull Run
steps.text: Confederate batteries bombarded Fort Sumter in Charleston harbour, and Lincoln called for volunteers, prompting four more states to secede. The first major battle, at Bull Run near Manassas, ended in a Union rout and showed the war would be long.

battles.name: Fort Sumter
battles.text: The Union garrison surrendered after a 34-hour bombardment, starting the war.

battles.name: First Battle of Bull Run
battles.text: Confederate reinforcements arrived by rail and turned the battle into a Union rout.

steps.label: Feb-Apr 1862
steps.title: War in the West
steps.text: Ulysses S. Grant captured Forts Henry and Donelson, opening Tennessee to Union armies, and survived a Confederate surprise attack at Shiloh. A Union fleet under David Farragut ran past the forts below New Orleans and took the South's largest city.

moves.label: Grant takes Forts Henry and Donelson

battles.name: Battle of Fort Donelson
battles.text: Grant forced the surrender of over 12,000 Confederates and earned the name Unconditional Surrender Grant.

battles.name: Battle of Shiloh
battles.text: Grant's army survived a surprise attack and drove the Confederates back in a battle of shocking losses.

battles.name: Capture of New Orleans
battles.text: Farragut's fleet captured New Orleans and closed the mouth of the Mississippi.

steps.label: Jun-Sep 1862
steps.title: Lee takes command; Antietam
steps.text: McClellan's army landed on the Virginia peninsula and neared Richmond, but Robert E. Lee drove it back in the Seven Days Battles and then beat another Union army at Second Bull Run. Lee invaded Maryland and was checked at Antietam, the bloodiest single day in American history, after which Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

battles.name: Seven Days Battles
battles.text: Lee's attacks drove McClellan's army away from Richmond.

battles.name: Second Battle of Bull Run
battles.text: Lee and Jackson routed John Pope's army.

battles.name: Battle of Antietam
battles.text: A tactically indecisive but strategic Union victory that ended Lee's first invasion of the North.

steps.label: May-Jul 1863
steps.title: Gettysburg and Vicksburg
steps.text: Lee won his greatest victory at Chancellorsville and invaded Pennsylvania, but was defeated at Gettysburg in three days of fighting. A day later Vicksburg surrendered to Grant after a brilliant campaign and siege, giving the Union control of the Mississippi and splitting the Confederacy.

battles.name: Battle of Chancellorsville
battles.text: Lee split his smaller army and routed Hooker, but Stonewall Jackson was mortally wounded.

battles.name: Battle of Gettysburg
battles.text: Meade's army repelled Lee's assaults, including Pickett's Charge, ending his invasion.

battles.name: Siege of Vicksburg
battles.text: Pemberton surrendered the fortress city and nearly 30,000 men on 4 July.

steps.label: Sep-Nov 1863
steps.title: Chickamauga and Chattanooga
steps.text: Rosecrans manoeuvred the Confederates out of Chattanooga, but Bragg, reinforced by Longstreet's corps sent by rail from Virginia, routed him at Chickamauga. Grant took command, broke the siege of Chattanooga and opened the gateway to Georgia.

battles.name: Battle of Chickamauga
battles.text: The largest Confederate victory in the West drove Rosecrans back into Chattanooga.

battles.name: Battle of Chattanooga
battles.text: Union troops stormed Missionary Ridge and routed Bragg's army.

steps.label: May-Jun 1864
steps.title: The Overland Campaign
steps.text: Grant, now commanding all Union armies, attacked Lee relentlessly in Virginia, suffering huge losses at the Wilderness, Spotsylvania and Cold Harbor but never retreating. He swung south of Richmond and pinned Lee in a long siege at Petersburg.

battles.name: Battle of the Wilderness
battles.text: Two days of fighting in dense, burning woods ended without a decision, but Grant pressed on.

battles.name: Battle of Spotsylvania Court House
battles.text: Two weeks of fighting around Lee's trenches, including the Bloody Angle, ended in stalemate.

battles.name: Battle of Cold Harbor
battles.text: A failed Union frontal assault cost thousands of men in a few hours.

steps.label: Sep-Dec 1864
steps.title: Atlanta and the March to the Sea
steps.text: Sherman captured Atlanta in September, helping secure Lincoln's re-election. He then cut loose from his supply lines and marched to Savannah, destroying railways and property, while Union forces destroyed Hood's army at Franklin and Nashville.

battles.name: Fall of Atlanta
battles.text: Sherman cut Atlanta's last railroad and Hood evacuated the city.

battles.name: Battle of Nashville
battles.text: Thomas shattered Hood's Army of Tennessee.

battles.name: Capture of Savannah
battles.text: Sherman reached the sea and took Savannah just before Christmas.

steps.label: Feb-Apr 1865
steps.title: Appomattox
steps.text: Sherman marched north through the Carolinas while Grant broke Lee's lines at Five Forks, forcing the evacuation of Petersburg and Richmond. Lee's starving army was cut off and surrendered at Appomattox Court House on 9 April; Lincoln was assassinated five days later and the remaining Confederate armies soon surrendered.

battles.name: Battle of Five Forks
battles.text: Sheridan's victory broke Lee's line and doomed Petersburg.

battles.name: Surrender at Appomattox Court House
battles.text: Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Grant.

name: World War I
summary: The Allied Powers, chiefly France, Britain, Russia, Italy and from 1917 the United States, fought the Central Powers of Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand set off a chain of alliances. Years of trench warfare and industrial killing ended with the Central Powers' defeat in 1918, after about 9 million soldiers had died. The war destroyed four empires, brought revolution to Russia and redrew the map of Europe and the Middle East.

steps.label: Aug-Sep 1914
steps.title: The Schlieffen Plan and the Marne
steps.text: Germany invaded neutral Belgium to outflank France, bringing Britain into the war. The German right wing swept toward Paris, but French and British counterattacks on the Marne forced it back, and both sides dug trenches from the Channel to Switzerland.

moves.label: Germans fall back to the Aisne

battles.name: Battle of Liege
battles.text: German siege guns reduced the Belgian forts, but the defence delayed the German timetable.

battles.name: First Battle of the Marne
battles.text: The Allied counterattack stopped the German advance short of Paris and ended hopes of a quick war.

steps.label: Aug-Sep 1914
steps.title: The Eastern Front opens
steps.text: Russia invaded East Prussia sooner than Germany expected, but its Second Army was encircled and destroyed at Tannenberg. Further south Russian armies routed the Austro-Hungarians in Galicia and took Lemberg.

battles.name: Battle of Tannenberg
battles.text: Hindenburg and Ludendorff encircled the Russian Second Army and took over 90,000 prisoners.

battles.name: Battle of Galicia
battles.text: Russia defeated Austria-Hungary, took Lemberg and besieged Przemysl.

steps.label: Apr 1915-Apr 1916
steps.title: Gallipoli and the Great Retreat
steps.text: Allied troops landed at Gallipoli to knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war but were pinned on the beaches and withdrew in January 1916. In the east a German and Austro-Hungarian breakthrough at Gorlice-Tarnow drove the Russians out of Poland, and in Mesopotamia a British force was besieged and captured at Kut.

battles.name: Gallipoli campaign
battles.text: Ottoman forces under Liman von Sanders and Mustafa Kemal held the peninsula and forced an Allied evacuation.

battles.name: Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive
battles.text: The Central Powers broke the Russian front and began a retreat of hundreds of kilometres.

battles.name: Siege of Kut
battles.text: About 13,000 British and Indian troops surrendered to the Ottomans after a five-month siege.

steps.label: Feb-Nov 1916
steps.title: Verdun, Jutland and the Somme
steps.text: Germany attacked Verdun to bleed France white, and the British and French launched the Somme offensive partly to relieve it; together the two battles cost well over a million casualties. The British and German fleets clashed at Jutland, and Russia's Brusilov Offensive smashed the Austro-Hungarian front.

battles.name: Battle of Verdun
battles.text: France held Verdun through ten months of fighting that killed around 300,000 men.

battles.name: Battle of Jutland
battles.text: Britain lost more ships, but the German fleet returned to port and the blockade held.

battles.name: Battle of the Somme
battles.text: Months of attritional fighting gained a few kilometres; the British suffered 57,000 casualties on the first day.

steps.title: Revolution and America enters
steps.text: Unrestricted German submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram brought the United States into the war in April. Russia was convulsed by two revolutions and the Bolsheviks sought peace, while the British slogged through Passchendaele, Italy collapsed at Caporetto and British forces took Jerusalem.

battles.name: Battle of Passchendaele
battles.text: British and Dominion troops took the ridge after months in deep mud at a cost of about 250,000 casualties.

battles.name: Battle of Caporetto
battles.text: An Austro-German attack routed the Italian army back to the Piave river.

battles.name: Battle of Beersheba
battles.text: Australian Light Horse charged and captured Beersheba, unlocking the Gaza line.

steps.label: Mar-Jul 1918
steps.title: Germany's last gamble
steps.text: After Russia signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, Germany moved divisions west and launched its Spring Offensive to win before American troops arrived in strength. The attacks gained more ground than any since 1914 but exhausted the German army, and the Second Battle of the Marne turned the tide.

battles.name: Operation Michael
battles.text: The German attack broke through on the Somme but stalled short of Amiens.

battles.name: Second Battle of the Marne
battles.text: French, American, British and Italian troops halted the last German offensive and counterattacked.

steps.label: Aug-Nov 1918
steps.title: The Hundred Days and the Armistice
steps.text: The Allies attacked along the whole Western Front, beginning at Amiens, and drove the Germans back through their defensive lines. Bulgaria, the Ottoman Empire and Austria-Hungary sued for peace, revolution broke out in Germany, and the Armistice took effect on 11 November 1918.

battles.name: Battle of Amiens
battles.text: A surprise tank-led attack that Ludendorff called the black day of the German army.

battles.name: Meuse-Argonne Offensive
battles.text: The largest American battle of the war pushed through the Argonne Forest toward Sedan.

battles.name: Battle of Megiddo
battles.text: Allenby's breakthrough destroyed the Ottoman armies in Palestine.

name: World War II
summary: The Allies, led by Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States and China, fought the Axis powers of Germany, Italy and Japan after German and Japanese wars of conquest in Europe and Asia. The Axis was defeated in Europe in May 1945 and Japan surrendered in August after the atomic bombings and Soviet entry into the war. The deadliest conflict in history, with 70 to 85 million dead including six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust, it left the United States and Soviet Union as rival superpowers.

steps.label: Sep 1939
steps.title: Invasion of Poland
steps.text: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September, and Britain and France declared war two days later. Under the Nazi-Soviet Pact the Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September, and Poland was partitioned within weeks.

moves.label: Army Group North from East Prussia

battles.name: Battle of the Bzura
battles.text: The largest battle of the campaign ended with the encirclement of the Polish Poznan and Pomorze armies.

battles.name: Siege of Warsaw
battles.text: Warsaw surrendered on 28 September after heavy bombing and shelling.

steps.label: Apr-Jun 1940
steps.title: Blitzkrieg in the West
steps.text: After seizing Denmark and Norway, Germany attacked the Netherlands, Belgium and France on 10 May. Panzer divisions broke through the Ardennes at Sedan and raced to the Channel, trapping Allied armies; most of the British force was evacuated from Dunkirk, and France signed an armistice on 22 June.

moves.label: Army Group B into the Low Countries
Panzers through the Ardennes to the Channel

battles.name: Battle of Sedan
battles.text: German panzers crossed the Meuse and broke the French front.

battles.name: Battle of Dunkirk
battles.text: The port fell, but about 338,000 Allied troops were evacuated to Britain.

steps.label: Jul 1940-Nov 1941
steps.title: Britain stands; war in the desert
steps.text: The Royal Air Force defeated the Luftwaffe's attempt to win air control over Britain, ending invasion plans, though the Blitz on British cities went on into 1941. In North Africa a small British force routed the Italians, then Rommel's Afrika Korps drove the British back to Egypt but could not take Tobruk.

battles.name: Battle of Britain
battles.text: Fighter Command beat the Luftwaffe in the skies over southern England.

battles.name: Battle of Beda Fomm
battles.text: British forces cut off and destroyed the retreating Italian Tenth Army.

battles.name: Siege of Tobruk
battles.text: Australian and other Allied troops held the port for eight months.

steps.label: Jun-Dec 1941
steps.title: Operation Barbarossa
steps.text: Germany and its allies invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June with over three million men, encircling whole Soviet armies and beginning the mass murder of Jews in the east. Leningrad was besieged and Kiev taken, but the Red Army stopped the Germans before Moscow and counterattacked in December.

battles.name: Battle of Kiev
battles.text: The Germans encircled and captured over 600,000 Soviet soldiers.

battles.name: Siege of Leningrad
battles.text: The city held out through a 872-day siege in which around a million civilians died.

battles.name: Battle of Moscow
battles.text: The Red Army halted the German drive on Moscow and threw it back in winter.

steps.label: Dec 1941-Jun 1942
steps.title: Pearl Harbor and Japan's advance
steps.text: Japan attacked the US fleet at Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 and swept through Malaya, the Philippines, the Dutch East Indies and Burma; Germany declared war on the United States. Singapore fell in February, but in June American carriers sank four Japanese carriers at Midway, turning the tide in the Pacific.

battles.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
battles.text: Japanese carrier aircraft sank or damaged eight US battleships and killed over 2,400 Americans.

battles.name: Fall of Singapore
battles.text: About 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops surrendered in Britain's worst defeat.

battles.name: Battle of Midway
battles.text: US carrier aircraft sank four Japanese fleet carriers north-west of Midway Atoll.

steps.label: Aug 1942-Feb 1943
steps.title: Turning points
steps.text: Germany's summer offensive drove toward Stalingrad and the Caucasus oil fields, but a Soviet counteroffensive encircled the German Sixth Army in the city. Montgomery won at El Alamein as Anglo-American forces landed in Morocco and Algeria, and US forces fought a long battle for Guadalcanal.

battles.name: Second Battle of El Alamein
battles.text: Montgomery's Eighth Army broke the German and Italian line and drove Rommel out of Egypt.

battles.name: Battle of Stalingrad
battles.text: The encircled German Sixth Army surrendered in February 1943 after months of street fighting.

battles.name: Guadalcanal campaign
battles.text: After six months of land, sea and air battles Japan evacuated the island.

steps.title: The Axis in retreat
steps.text: Axis forces in Tunisia surrendered in May, and the Allies invaded Sicily in July, leading to Mussolini's fall and Italy's armistice in September. The last great German offensive in the east failed at Kursk, and the Red Army advanced to the Dnieper and retook Kiev.

battles.name: Tunisian campaign
battles.text: About 250,000 German and Italian troops surrendered in Tunisia.

battles.name: Battle of Kursk
battles.text: The Soviet defence and counteroffensive defeated the last major German offensive in the east.

battles.name: Invasion of Sicily
battles.text: Allied landings conquered Sicily in 38 days and toppled Mussolini.

steps.label: Jun-Aug 1944
steps.title: D-Day and Operation Bagration
steps.text: On 6 June 1944 the Western Allies landed in Normandy in the largest seaborne invasion in history, broke out in August and liberated Paris. Weeks later the Soviet Operation Bagration destroyed German Army Group Centre and carried the Red Army to the Vistula.

battles.name: Normandy landings
battles.text: American, British and Canadian troops stormed five beaches and established a front in France.

battles.name: Operation Bagration
battles.text: The Red Army destroyed German Army Group Centre and liberated Belarus.

battles.name: Liberation of Paris
battles.text: French and American troops entered Paris on 25 August.

steps.label: Jun 1944-Mar 1945
steps.title: Island-hopping in the Pacific
steps.text: US forces advanced across the central Pacific to the Marianas, bringing Japan within reach of B-29 bombers, while MacArthur moved along New Guinea. The return to the Philippines brought the Battle of Leyte Gulf, the largest naval battle in history, and in early 1945 Marines took Iwo Jima.

battles.name: Battle of Saipan
battles.text: US forces captured Saipan, and the nearby Battle of the Philippine Sea crippled Japanese naval air power.

battles.name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
battles.text: The US Navy destroyed much of the remaining Japanese fleet.

battles.name: Battle of Iwo Jima
battles.text: US Marines took the island after five weeks of fighting against entrenched defenders.

steps.label: Apr-Sep 1945
steps.title: Defeat of Germany and Japan
steps.text: Soviet armies stormed Berlin while American and British forces crossed Germany and met the Red Army on the Elbe; Hitler killed himself and Germany surrendered on 8 May. After the costly fight for Okinawa, the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the Soviet Union invaded Manchuria, and Japan surrendered on 2 September.

moves.label: Soviets into Manchuria from the east

battles.name: Battle of Berlin
battles.text: The Red Army captured Berlin, and the city's garrison surrendered on 2 May.

battles.name: Battle of Okinawa
battles.text: An 82-day battle killed over 100,000 Japanese soldiers and a huge number of Okinawan civilians.

battles.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria
battles.text: Soviet forces overran Japan's Kwantung Army in under two weeks.

name: Korean War
summary: North Korea, backed by the Soviet Union and later joined by Chinese troops, invaded South Korea, which was defended by the United States and a United Nations coalition. After dramatic swings up and down the peninsula the war settled into a stalemate near the 38th parallel, and an armistice in 1953 left Korea divided. Millions died, and the war hardened Cold War divisions in Asia that persist today.

steps.label: Jun-Sep 1950
steps.title: North Korea invades
steps.text: On 25 June 1950 the North Korean army crossed the 38th parallel and captured Seoul within days. The UN Security Council authorised military help, but US and South Korean forces were pushed back into a perimeter around Busan.

battles.name: First Battle of Seoul
battles.text: North Korean forces captured the South Korean capital three days into the war.

battles.name: Battle of Daejeon
battles.text: The US 24th Division delayed the advance but lost the city and its commander was captured.

battles.name: Battle of the Pusan Perimeter
battles.text: UN forces held the line of the Naktong River for six weeks.

steps.label: Sep 1950
steps.title: The Inchon landing
steps.text: MacArthur landed a US corps far behind enemy lines at Inchon on 15 September, cutting North Korean supply lines. UN forces broke out of the Busan perimeter and recaptured Seoul by the end of the month.

battles.name: Battle of Inchon
battles.text: A bold amphibious landing turned the course of the war.

battles.name: Second Battle of Seoul
battles.text: US Marines and South Korean troops retook the capital after street fighting.

steps.label: Oct-Nov 1950
steps.title: UN advance to the Yalu
