steps.text: UN forces crossed the 38th parallel to unify Korea, took Pyongyang and pushed toward the Chinese border on the Yalu. China, warning against the advance, secretly sent large forces into Korea and struck the first blows at Unsan.

moves.label: X Corps by sea to Wonsan
X Corps toward the Chosin Reservoir

battles.name: Capture of Pyongyang
battles.text: UN forces took the North Korean capital on 19 October.

battles.name: Battle of Unsan
battles.text: Chinese troops mauled US and South Korean units in their first major attack.

steps.label: Nov 1950-Jan 1951
steps.title: China intervenes
steps.text: Massive Chinese offensives in bitter cold routed the Eighth Army on the Chongchon River and surrounded US Marines at the Chosin Reservoir, who fought their way out to the coast. UN forces retreated south of the 38th parallel, and Seoul fell again in January 1951.

battles.name: Battle of the Chongchon River
battles.text: Chinese attacks broke the Eighth Army and forced the longest retreat in US Army history.

battles.name: Battle of Chosin Reservoir
battles.text: US Marines and soldiers broke out of encirclement in brutal cold, but China regained northeast Korea.

battles.name: Third Battle of Seoul
battles.text: Chinese and North Korean forces recaptured Seoul in January 1951.

steps.label: Feb-May 1951
steps.title: Counteroffensives
steps.text: Under General Ridgway, UN forces held at Chipyong-ni and pushed north again, retaking Seoul in March. China's spring offensive in April and May was stopped short of Seoul, and the front stabilised near the 38th parallel.

battles.name: Battle of Chipyong-ni
battles.text: Surrounded US and French troops held off Chinese attacks, restoring UN morale.

battles.name: Battle of Kapyong
battles.text: Commonwealth troops blunted the Chinese spring offensive in the centre.

steps.label: Jul 1951-1953
steps.title: Stalemate and the hill battles
steps.text: Armistice talks opened at Kaesong and moved to Panmunjom while both sides fought costly battles for hills along a fortified front. The fate of prisoners who did not want to go home was the main sticking point in the talks.

battles.name: Battle of Heartbreak Ridge
battles.text: UN forces took the ridge after a month of fighting with heavy losses.

battles.name: Battle of Triangle Hill
battles.text: Chinese forces held their positions after six weeks of fighting.

steps.label: Jul 1953
steps.title: Armistice
steps.text: A final Chinese offensive at Kumsong pushed back South Korean lines weeks before the armistice was signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953. It created the Demilitarized Zone near the 38th parallel; no peace treaty has ever been signed.

battles.name: Battle of Kumsong
battles.text: The last major Chinese offensive gained ground before the ceasefire.

name: Vietnam War
summary: Communist North Vietnam and the southern Viet Cong insurgency fought South Vietnam and its chief ally the United States to reunify the country under communist rule. US combat troops arrived in 1965 and withdrew in 1973 after a costly, divisive war, and North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon in April 1975. Millions of Vietnamese and over 58,000 Americans died, and the war reshaped US foreign policy and society.

steps.title: Two Vietnams and a growing insurgency
steps.text: The 1954 Geneva Accords split Vietnam at the 17th parallel, and Ngo Dinh Diem founded the Republic of Vietnam in the south in 1955, blocking planned reunification elections. Hanoi backed a southern insurgency, the National Liberation Front or Viet Cong, supplied along the Ho Chi Minh Trail, while US military advisers grew to about 16,000 by 1963.

battles.name: Battle of Ap Bac
battles.text: A Viet Cong battalion beat off a much larger South Vietnamese force with US advisers.

steps.label: Aug 1964-1965
steps.title: Tonkin Gulf and American escalation
steps.text: After a clash between US destroyers and North Vietnamese boats, Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution. In 1965 the US began sustained bombing of the North and landed Marines at Da Nang, and US troop numbers rose to over 180,000 by the end of the year.

moves.label: US Marines land at Da Nang

battles.name: Gulf of Tonkin incident
battles.text: North Vietnamese torpedo boats attacked USS Maddox; a second reported attack two days later probably never happened.

battles.name: Battle of Ia Drang
battles.text: The first major battle between US and North Vietnamese regular troops; both sides claimed success.

steps.label: Jan-Apr 1968
steps.title: The Tet Offensive
steps.text: During the Tet holiday the Viet Cong and North Vietnamese attacked over 100 towns and cities, including the US embassy in Saigon. The offensive was beaten back with very heavy communist losses, but it shocked the American public and led President Johnson to limit bombing and seek talks.

battles.name: Siege of Khe Sanh
battles.text: The Marine base held through a 77-day siege and was abandoned a few months later.

battles.name: Battle of Hue
battles.text: US and South Vietnamese troops retook the old imperial city after nearly a month of street fighting.

battles.name: Tet attacks on Saigon
battles.text: Attackers in Saigon were defeated within days, but the shock was enormous.

steps.title: Vietnamization and widening war
steps.text: President Nixon began withdrawing US troops while handing the fighting to the South Vietnamese army. US and South Vietnamese forces struck Viet Cong bases in Cambodia in 1970, and a South Vietnamese incursion into Laos in 1971 was driven back.

battles.name: Battle of Hamburger Hill
battles.text: US troops took the hill after ten days of costly assaults, then abandoned it.

battles.name: Operation Lam Son 719
battles.text: South Vietnamese forces reached Tchepone in Laos but retreated under heavy attack.

steps.label: Mar-Oct 1972
steps.title: The Easter Offensive
steps.text: North Vietnam launched a conventional invasion across the DMZ and from Laos and Cambodia, using tanks and artillery. South Vietnamese forces, backed by massive US air power, held An Loc and Kontum and retook Quang Tri.

battles.name: Battle of Quang Tri
battles.text: The city fell in May and South Vietnamese troops retook its ruins in September.

battles.name: Battle of An Loc
battles.text: The besieged town held for two months, blocking the road to Saigon.

battles.name: Battle of Kontum
battles.text: South Vietnamese troops and US bombers held the Central Highlands city.

steps.label: Jan-Mar 1973
steps.title: Paris Peace Accords
steps.text: After the heavy Christmas bombing of Hanoi and Haiphong, the Paris Peace Accords were signed in January 1973. The last US combat troops left in March and American prisoners were released, but North Vietnamese troops remained in the South and fighting soon resumed.

steps.label: Mar-Apr 1975
steps.title: Fall of Saigon
steps.text: North Vietnam's final offensive began in the Central Highlands at Ban Me Thuot, and a disorderly South Vietnamese retreat lost Hue and Da Nang. After the last stand at Xuan Loc, North Vietnamese tanks entered Saigon on 30 April 1975, and the country was reunified in 1976.

battles.name: Battle of Ban Me Thuot
battles.text: The surprise capture of the city triggered the collapse of the South Vietnamese army.

battles.name: Battle of Xuan Loc
battles.text: South Vietnam's 18th Division held for nearly two weeks before withdrawing.

battles.name: Fall of Saigon
battles.text: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon and South Vietnam surrendered.

name: Russia-Ukraine War
summary: Russia and Ukraine have been at war since 2014, when Russia annexed Crimea and backed armed separatists in the Donbas after Ukraine's pro-Western Euromaidan revolution. In February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion that failed to take Kyiv and became a war of attrition along a long front in the east and south. At the end of 2025 fighting continued without a ceasefire, in the largest war in Europe since 1945.

steps.label: Feb-Mar 2014
steps.title: Annexation of Crimea
steps.text: After protests in Kyiv led to the ouster of President Viktor Yanukovych, Russian troops without insignia took control of Crimea. A referendum held under Russian control and rejected as illegitimate by Ukraine and most UN members was followed by Russia's annexation of the peninsula on 18 March 2014.

steps.label: Apr 2014-Feb 2015
steps.title: War in the Donbas
steps.text: Armed separatists backed by Russia seized government buildings and towns in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, and Ukraine launched military operations against them. In August 2014 Russian regular units crossed the border and defeated Ukrainian forces at Ilovaisk, and the Minsk agreements of 2014 and 2015 froze but did not end the fighting.

battles.name: Battle of Ilovaisk
battles.text: Ukrainian units were encircled and suffered heavy losses during their withdrawal.

battles.name: Second Battle of Donetsk Airport
battles.text: Ukrainian defenders held the ruined airport for months before withdrawing in January 2015.

battles.name: Battle of Debaltseve
battles.text: Ukrainian forces withdrew from the rail hub days after the second Minsk agreement.

steps.title: A frozen front
steps.text: Trench warfare and shelling continued along a line of contact in the Donbas, and by early 2022 over 14,000 people had been killed since 2014. In 2018 Russia opened a bridge to Crimea and seized Ukrainian naval vessels near the Kerch Strait, and in 2021 it massed troops near Ukraine's borders.

battles.name: Kerch Strait incident
battles.text: Russian forces fired on and seized three Ukrainian naval vessels and their crews.

steps.label: Feb-Apr 2022
steps.title: Full-scale invasion
steps.text: On 24 February 2022 Russia invaded from Belarus, Russia and Crimea. Ukrainian forces stopped the assault on Kyiv and Russia withdrew from the north by early April, but Russian troops took Kherson and much of the south and besieged Mariupol.

battles.name: Battle of Kyiv
battles.text: Ukrainian forces halted the Russian advance in the city's outskirts, and Russia withdrew from the north.

battles.name: Battle of Kharkiv
battles.text: Russian forces failed to take Ukraine's second-largest city.

battles.name: Siege of Mariupol
battles.text: Russian forces took the devastated city after the last defenders at the Azovstal steelworks surrendered in May.

steps.label: Sep-Nov 2022
steps.title: Ukrainian counteroffensives
steps.text: A rapid Ukrainian offensive in September recaptured most of Kharkiv oblast, and Russia announced a partial mobilisation and claimed to annex four Ukrainian oblasts, a claim most states reject. In November Russian forces withdrew across the Dnipro and Ukraine retook Kherson city.

battles.name: Kharkiv counteroffensive
battles.text: Ukrainian forces broke through and retook Izium, Kupiansk and thousands of square kilometres.

battles.name: Liberation of Kherson
battles.text: Russian forces withdrew from the only regional capital they had captured since February.

steps.title: Bakhmut and the summer counteroffensive
steps.text: Russian forces, including Wagner Group fighters, captured Bakhmut in May after months of extremely costly fighting. Ukraine's summer counteroffensive in Zaporizhzhia oblast met dense minefields and made only small gains, and the Kakhovka dam was destroyed in June.

battles.name: Battle of Bakhmut
battles.text: Russian forces took the ruined city after about ten months of fighting.

battles.name: Zaporizhzhia counteroffensive
battles.text: Ukraine recaptured Robotyne and nearby villages but did not break the Russian defences.

steps.title: Avdiivka, Kursk and Pokrovsk
steps.text: Russia took Avdiivka in February and pressed slow, costly advances in Donetsk oblast toward Pokrovsk. In August Ukraine launched a surprise cross-border incursion into Russia's Kursk oblast, and North Korean troops were later deployed to help Russia push it back.

battles.name: Battle of Avdiivka
battles.text: Ukrainian forces withdrew from the heavily fortified town in February 2024.

battles.name: Kursk incursion
battles.text: Ukraine seized Sudzha and nearby areas; Russian forces retook most of the territory by March 2025.

steps.title: Attrition and diplomacy
steps.text: Russian forces continued slow advances in Donetsk oblast, fighting for Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad and pushing toward Kostiantynivka, while both sides struck each other's cities and energy infrastructure with drones and missiles. US-led diplomacy produced talks and several peace proposals, but no ceasefire had been agreed by the end of 2025.

battles.name: Battle of Pokrovsk
battles.text: Russian forces fought into the city through 2025; control was still contested at the end of the year.
